e-9454.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Velocity
e-9454.problem:
A body of mass $3 \, \textrm{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\textrm{N}).$
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t) =t^2- e^{t-4}$ meters per second.
Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=4$ seconds.
e-9454.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-{e}^{t-4}) \\  & =2t-{e}^{t-4}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=4 \, \textrm{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =2(4)-{e}^{4-4} \\  & =8-1 \\  & =7\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =3\cdot (7) \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F| = |21| = 21 \, \textrm{N}.
$$

e-9859.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Displacement
e-9859.problem:
A body of mass $2 \, \textrm{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t) = e^{3t-6} + t^2$ meters. Find the expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
e-9859.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t-6}+{t}^{2}) \\  & =3{e}^{3t-6}+2t\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{e}^{3t-6}+2t) \\  & =9{e}^{3t-6}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force acting on the body, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =2\cdot (9{e}^{3t-6}+2) \\  & =18{e}^{3t-6}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9860.knowledge_point: Determining Moments When a Force Has Zero Magnitude
e-9860.problem:
A body of mass $2 \, \textrm{kg}$ moves in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\geq 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t) =2t^3-12t^2-30t+5$ meters per second.
Calculate the time when the force acting on the body has a magnitude of zero.
e-9860.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-12{t}^{2}-30t+5) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-24t-30\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{t}^{2}-24t-30 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-4t-5 & =0 \\ (t+1)(t-5) & =0 \\ t & =-1,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t \geq 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude when $t=5 \, \textrm{s}.$

after.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{e}^{\frac{t}{2}}) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{\frac{t}{2}}) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{\frac{t}{2}} \\  & =2{e}^{\frac{t}{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =2{e}^{\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}} \\  & =2{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =2(3) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =ma(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 6 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3)|=|1|=1\,\text{N}.

$$

$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
A body of mass $1.5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)={t}^{4}-{t}^{3}$ meters.
Find the expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-{t}^{3}) \\  & =4{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}) \\  & =12{t}^{2}-6t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =1.5\cdot (12{t}^{2}-6t) \\  & =18{t}^{2}-9t.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.

Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.
content.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-36t+2) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-6t-36\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{t}^{2}-6t-36 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-t-6 & =0 \\ (t-3)(t+2) & =0 \\ t & =-2,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution.
